title: Building voice agents with OpenAI — Dominik Kundel, OpenAI
talk_summary: A live-coding workshop on OpenAI's Agents SDK for voice agents, covering chained vs speech-to-speech architectures, real-time sessions, tools, handoffs, guardrails, and human-in-the-loop approval.

takeaways.technique: Frontline agent delegates heavy reasoning to a stronger backend agent via tool call
takeaways.what_they_do: A fast, cheap frontline agent handles the interaction and calls a tool that runs a separate, smarter reasoning model (o4-mini) on the server, returning the result; the two agents share the same SDK and full transcript context.

Prompt the agent to say what it is about to do before calling a slow tool, so the tool call completes while the previous output is still being consumed; also split long tasks into start-task + poll-status tools so the model isn't blocked.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you want to find ways to do things like buying yourself some time. So you will typically see some prompting around like announce what you're about to do next

takeaways.technique: Handoffs that reset agent config (instructions + tools) per subtask
takeaways.what_they_do: A handoff is a specialized tool call that swaps the active agent's system instructions and tool set mid-session, scoping each agent to one narrow task instead of one giant prompt.

takeaways.technique: Output guardrails run in parallel on the transcript, with policy hints
takeaways.what_they_do: Guardrails run continuously over the transcript (configurable frequency) and can interrupt output; when violated they pass a policy hint telling the model why it failed and what to do instead.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can give it um policy hints essentially on like why it violated this policy or what it should do instead

takeaways.technique: Keep raw artifacts (audio/transcripts) and replay them for evals; human review as first eval
takeaways.what_they_do: Persist the raw interaction artifacts and replay them when iterating; use human review of real traces plus a predetermined example set as the initial eval before launch.
Tools can require approval (always or via a predicate) before execution; the request is intercepted before side effects, avoiding rollback of partial actions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the model is asking for this tool to be executed but we're intercepting this um basically before we're ever generating or executing the response
